title: Bring evidence to a contested decision
why_matters: Halfway through the second half of your probation, you should be able to do more than collect requirements — you should be able to shape a decision with data. Pick a contested decision the team is currently making by gut and bring even one piece of evidence that re-frames it. This is what shifts you from analyst to trusted analyst.
steps: Find one open decision the team has been going back-and-forth on without resolving. Could be technical, process, or business-side.
Identify what evidence would actually help. Sometimes it's a number; sometimes it's a worked example; sometimes it's a precedent from another team or industry.
Get the evidence. Write it up in half a page — what the data says, what it doesn't say, what would change if it were different.
Bring it into the room (or the thread) where the decision is being argued. Don't tell people what to decide; tell them what the evidence shows.
success_criteria: A half-page evidence document exists. It has been brought into the relevant conversation. The conversation has changed in a way you can describe in one sentence.
reflection_prompt: What's the strongest argument against the conclusion the evidence pointed to, and did you account for it?
